explanation: A pit between each eye and nostril senses infrared, giving the snake a heat picture of prey. Pythons and some boas have heat pits too, along their lips.

claims.text: Pit vipers, including rattlesnakes, detect the body heat (infrared radiation) of warm-blooded prey with pit organs.
Snakes do not echolocate, hear heartbeats or sense electric fields to find prey.
A pit viper's heat-sensing pits are located between the eye and the nostril on each side of the head.
Pythons and some boas have heat-sensing pits along their lips.
